mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in mortgage applications (HOUST) signals weakening household demand and housing market stress, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a coordinated global demand shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, driving higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the pattern reverses during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a global supply chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary-inflationary tightening, which raises real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while personal income growth (PAYEMS) lags GDP growth (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, implying lower near-term consumption and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA AND PAYEMS growth < GDPC1 growth for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a fiscal stimulus rollout.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a technology-driven earnings surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average while GDP growth remains positive signals a housing market contraction that depresses construction-related earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-mo MA AND GDPC1 growth > 0% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: housing market downturn with overall growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a coordinated global housing recovery.
